statement.p: Consider the vectors \vec a = 3\,\mathit{\vec i}+\,\mathit{\vec j}-\,\mathit{\vec k}, \qquad \vec b = 3 \vec{i} - \vec{j} + \vec{k}, \qquad \vec c = -\,\mathit{\vec i}-3\,\mathit{\vec j}+\,\mathit{\vec k} \vec d = \,\mathit{\vec i}+0.333333\,\mathit{\vec j}+0.333333\,\mathit{\vec k},\qquad \vec g = \,\mathit{\vec i}-3\,\mathit{\vec j}. Which pairs (if any) of these vectors are

p.em: (Enter none or a pair or list of pairs, e.g., if \vec a is perpendicular to \vec b and \vec c, enter (a,b),(a,c).)
(Enter none or a pair or list of pairs, e.g., if \vec a is parallel to \vec b and \vec c, enter (a,b),(a,c).)

statement.p: (c) Have an angles less than \pi/2 between them?

p.em: (Enter none or a pair or list of pairs, e.g., if \vec a is at an angle less than pi/2 from \vec b and \vec c, enter (a,b),(a,c).)

statement.p: (d) Have an angle of more than \pi/2 between them?

p.em: (Enter none or a pair or list of pairs, e.g., if \vec a is at an angle greater than pi/2 from \vec b and \vec c, enter (a,b),(a,c).)

static.solution:
(a) Perpendicular vectors have a dot product of 0. Since \vec a\cdot\vec g = (3)\cdot(1) + (1)\cdot(-3) + (-1)\cdot(0) = 0 and similarly \vec d\cdot\vec g = 0, the pairs we want are (\vec a, \vec g), (\vec d, \vec g).
(b) Parallel vectors are multiples of one another. Since this is not the case for any of the pairs of vectors here, there are no parallel pairs.
(c) Since \vec v\cdot\vec w= \Vert\vec v\Vert \Vert\vec w\Vert\cos\theta, the dot product of the vectors we want is positive. Since \vec a\cdot\vec b = (3)\cdot(3) + (1)\cdot(-1) + (-1)\cdot(1) > 0 and similarly \vec a\cdot\vec d > 0, \vec b\cdot\vec c > 0, \vec b\cdot\vec d > 0, \vec b\cdot\vec g > 0, \vec c\cdot\vec g > 0, the pairs we want are (\vec a, \vec b), (\vec a, \vec d), (\vec b, \vec c), (\vec b, \vec d), (\vec b, \vec g), (\vec c, \vec g).
(d) Vectors with an angle of more than \pi/2 between them have a negative dot product. Since \vec a\cdot\vec c = (3)\cdot(-1) + (1)\cdot(-3) + (-1)\cdot(1) \lt 0 and similarly \vec c\cdot\vec d \lt 0, the pairs we want are (\vec a, \vec c), (\vec c, \vec d).
